summary: NYC311 separates neighbor noise from other noise categories and lists building management and mediation as additional routes.
tip: Note whether the sound is music, speech, or furniture movement; the city routes different sources differently.

summary: Portland’s Noise Program prioritizes specific dates, times and detailed descriptions and explains which noise types fall outside its authority.
tip: Describe a repeatable pattern and the source if you can identify it; vague reports may not be processed.

summary: Seattle Police distinguishes residential disturbances from other unreasonable noise. Different conditions apply to each category.
tip: Separate a house party from mechanical equipment and check the source-specific guidance before reporting.

summary: DC’s Office of Unified Communications lists noise complaints among police non-emergencies handled through its current contact guidance.
tip: Identify whether this is music, an animal or construction so your notes support the correct routing.

summary: Philadelphia distinguishes commercial and industrial noise handled by Air Management Services from individual or residential sources.
tip: Record whether the suspected source is a business, building equipment, or a residence; do not assume one contact handles all three.

summary: Austin’s guidance distinguishes mechanical noise and provides a route through Austin 3-1-1. Other complaints may follow different processes.
tip: For equipment, describe a fan, compressor or other observable source rather than guessing which neighbor caused it.

summary: San Diego’s police guidance addresses noisy neighbors, ongoing noise and mediation. It directs barking-dog issues through a different process.
tip: Write whether the sound is still occurring and keep each incident separate from your description of the overall pattern.

summary: Phoenix’s Law Department FAQ distinguishes non-emergency noise issues from property-code concerns and landlord–tenant disputes.
tip: Keep the sound observations factual; a noise log alone does not resolve a separate landlord–tenant question.

summary: Houston’s Chapter 30 FAQ explains sound regulation and complaint handling, including how official measurements are taken.
tip: Write where you placed your phone. Your indoor reference reading is different from an official measurement at a specified location.

summary: Minneapolis publishes separate guidance for construction, garbage collection, amplified sound and yard maintenance.
tip: Classify the source first and use the city’s matching section; do not apply construction rules to every household sound.

summary: Raleigh’s public-nuisance guidance identifies its police department as the contact for noise complaints.
tip: Include the local date and whether the noise is recurring. Check the current city process rather than relying on a saved phone number.

summary: Los Angeles separates general MyLA311 services from non-emergency police complaints, including noise.
tip: Distinguish a city-service request from a current noise disturbance and follow the city’s relevant channel.
